data.name: Heading

data.name: RequestAgency
data.value: Request a DDI Agency Identifier

data.name: RequestAgencyIntro
data.value: Follow these steps to obtain a DDI agency identifier.

data.name: HelpStep1
data.value: Create an account for your organization.

data.name: RegisterHere
data.value: Register here

data.name: NavigateTo
data.value: Navigate to the

data.name: Manage
data.value: Manage

data.name: WebSiteSection
data.value: section of the web site.

data.name: HelpStep3
data.value: Click the "Request New Agency" link to request your agency. See below for details on each field.

data.name: HelpStep4
data.value: You will receive an email confirmation when the agency identifier is approved.

data.name: AgencyName
data.value: Agency Name

data.name: AgencyNameBody
data.value: The agency name should be in the form [country code] dot [name]. For example: us.agencyname

data.name: ContactPersons
data.value: Types of Contact Persons

data.name: AdminContact
data.value: Administrative Contact

data.name: AdminContactBody
data.value: An administrative contact is the individual authorized to interact with the DDI Registry on behalf of the registrant specified in the WHOIS record. The administrative contact for your domain has the authorization to accept notices and make requests to the DDI Registry regarding the management of your agency identifier and, along with the technical contact for your agency identifier, will receive all renewal and other administrative notices associated with the agency identifier.

data.name: TechContact
data.value: Technical Contact

data.name: TechContactBody
data.value: The technical contact for your agency identifier is the individual or organization authorized to manage any technical issues related to your agency identifier.

data.name: SubAgency
data.value: Configure a Sub Agency

data.name: SubAgencyBody
data.value: Once your agency is approved, you can manage sub agencies. Sub agency identifiers are just like agency identifiers, but you can create them without waiting for approval.

data.name: SubAgencyStep2
data.value: Click the Manage link next to your approved agency identifier.

data.name: SubAgencyStep3
data.value: Click the "Add sub agency assignment" link.

data.name: SubAgencyStep4
data.value: Enter an identifier for your sub agency.

data.name: Resolution
data.value: Configure Resolution Services

data.name: ResolutionBody1
data.value: The DDI Registry integrates with the

data.name: DomainNameSystem
data.value: Domain Name System

data.name: ResolutionBody2
data.value: to provide global resolution for DDI-related services you may run. For example, you may allow people to query for the URL of a Web Service-based repository that holds your agency's metadata.

data.name: ResolutionStep3
data.value: Click the Edit link next to one of your sub agency identifiers.

data.name: ResolutionStep4
data.value: Click the "Add a service" link to describe the service for which you would like to enable resolution. If you would like to use your own DNS servers for resolution, use the Delegations section to configure your name servers.
